messages:
Talia Benson: just got notes back from the GCP Cloud Marketplace reviewer. TL;DR they’re confused by our SKU taxonomy and asked for a clarification call. :facepalm:

Talia Benson: key feedback bullets (paraphrased from partner portal):
- They can’t tell what’s a “plan” vs an “add-on” vs a separate “product”.
- Dedicated vs Private reads like two different solutions, but we’re presenting them as SKUs under one umbrella.
- “Compliance / Retention / Premium SLA” add-ons: reviewer asked whether these are separate billable line items in Marketplace or just feature tiers.
- They want consistent names across: listing plan names, billing descriptors, and the onboarding steps in docs.

Soojin Lee: ugh ok. did they say *what* format they want? (separate listings vs one listing with multiple plans?)

Talia Benson: they didn’t hard-reject, but the comment was basically “current structure is unclear to buyers + reviewers.” they asked us to “simplify plan structure and align to a single deployment model per plan.”

Camila Reyes: this tracks with what GCP has been picky about historically. they really hate when it feels like a menu of unrelated things.

Nikhil Sharma: for Hosted API we should keep it dead simple: “Pay-as-you-go (hosted)” and everything else as enterprise contact? or are we committed to listing Dedicated/Private as purchasable plans too?

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated is a real marketplace motion for some of my accounts (they want committed spend through GCP). but we need to present it as a plan with clear deliverable: “reserved capacity managed by Redwood” vs “self-serve API.”

Vivek Kulkarni: Private is probably what’s confusing them most. private = customer VPC / network isolation, but still “managed service” on our side. if the listing reads like “on-prem software” or “deploy into your project,” GCP will get twitchy.

Naomi Feldman: also on the compliance add-ons: we should be careful with language. if they’re separate SKUs/plans, we must ensure the marketplace plan description doesn’t imply SOC2 report is “publicly downloadable” etc.

Soojin Lee: what exact strings did they flag?

Talia Benson: they called out examples (again paraphrase):
- “Redwood Dedicated – Enterprise” vs “Redwood Private – VPC” vs “Hosted API – Pro”
They said the mix of “deployment words” + “tier words” makes it hard to understand what you’re buying.

Michael Grant: from legal/terms side: GCP Marketplace plan names should not imply additional contractual guarantees unless those are actually in the marketplace order form. “Premium SLA” as a marketplace line item is tricky unless the SLA terms are attached.

Laura Bennett: finance note: if we model add-ons as separate marketplace plans, we need to ensure customers can’t accidentally double-purchase or end up with mismatched entitlements. reviewer confusion is a red flag for billing confusion later.

Nikhil Sharma: suggestion: stop calling them SKUs in the listing copy. call them “Plans” with nouns:
- Hosted API (Pay-as-you-go)
- Dedicated Capacity (Committed)
- Private Deployment (Committed)
Then “Compliance Pack / Log Retention / Premium SLA” are “Add-ons (contact sales)” unless GCP supports add-on line items cleanly.

Soojin Lee: +1. and we should align the first line of each plan to a 1-sentence “what you get” statement.

Vivek Kulkarni: if we keep Private as a plan, we should explicitly say “Redwood-managed control plane + customer-managed networking (VPC/VPC-SC compatible)” and avoid wording that implies they deploy a VM or helm chart from marketplace.

Talia Benson: reviewer also asked: “If a buyer chooses Private, what is provisioned automatically by Marketplace vs manual onboarding?”

Lauren Bishop: that’s fair. for Dedicated/Private there’s human-in-the-loop anyway. maybe that’s another reason they want simplification.

Camila Reyes: can we do the call this week? i’d rather unblock now than iterate in comments forever.

Talia Benson: yes. they offered 30 mins. i can do Thu 11:00am PT or Fri 9:30am PT.

Soojin Lee: Thu 11 works for me.

Vivek Kulkarni: Thu 11 ok.

Lauren Bishop: Thu 11 ok.

Naomi Feldman: i can join for the first 15 mins if we’re talking compliance language.

Michael Grant: same, i can pop in if SLA/add-on wording comes up.

Talia Benson: great, i’ll confirm Thu 11am PT with GCP reviewer and send invite.

Talia Benson: action items before the call:
1) Soojin + Camila: propose simplified plan naming + 2-3 bullets per plan (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
2) Vivek + Lauren + Nikhil: confirm what’s actually purchasable as marketplace plans vs “sold separately” (esp add-ons).
3) Naomi: provide approved wording for compliance/retention/SLA that doesn’t over-promise.
4) Michael: sanity check on whether “Premium SLA” can be represented as a plan name in marketplace.

Soojin Lee: noted. i’ll draft copy that avoids “Enterprise/Pro” tier labels and focuses on deployment model + billing model.

Laura Bennett: pls also consider how it will appear on invoices. if plan name is too generic, customers/procurement get mad.

Talia Benson: good call. we’ll keep names simple but descriptive (and consistent w internal invoice descriptors).

Vivek Kulkarni: can we add a single “Which plan should I choose?” section in the listing FAQ to reduce reviewer confusion? e.g. decision tree.

Camila Reyes: yes but keep it short. reviewers hate walls of text.

Talia Benson: ok. i’ll drop a doc stub in the listing draft after the call (don’t want to churn twice).

Soojin Lee: :eyes: also please paste the exact reviewer quote if you have it (even screenshot) so we don’t misinterpret.

Talia Benson: will do (need to redact contact info). will post in thread in a bit.

Talia Benson: (follow-up) just uploaded a redacted snippet from the portal into the partner feedback log. the main line was: “Current plan/SKU naming mixes deployment types and add-ons; please simplify and clarify what is provisioned vs requires manual onboarding.”

Naomi Feldman: that “provisioned vs manual” question is actually helpful. we should answer that explicitly and consistently in docs + console.

Talia Benson: agreed. ok i’ll send the calendar invite once GCP confirms Thu time. :thumbsup:
